newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vebacom says Telekom price suit goes on.
newsitem.headline: Vebacom says Telekom price suit goes on.

text.p: German telephone venture Vebacom GmbH denied a newspaper report on Thursday that it would drop a complaint against Deutsche Telekom AG for anti-competitive pricing.
Vebacom has complained to the European Union about price rebates Telekom offers to corporate phone customers but not to other telephone providers who use its network.
"The complaint will be maintained," a company spokesman said.
The Berliner Zeitung said Vebacom had agreed to drop the complaint in exchange for a reduction in the fees Vebacom pays to Telekom to connect to its nationwide network.
The paper said agreement was reached in a December 20 meeting between Telekom chief Ron Sommer and Vebacom head Herbert Kraemer.
The Vebacom spokesman confirmed the executives met, but said they only discussed conditions for linking phone systems.
Competitors have to connect to Telekom's network because the former state monopoly controls cables running into customers' homes and offices.

Telekom last year offered 40 percent price cuts to its largest corporate customers. Vebacom then joined with the telecom units of Mannesmann AG and Thyssen AG to complain that they should qualify for rebates.
They lease phone lines from Telekom and pay fees to connect their own lines to Telekom's network.
Vebacom is a joint venture between utility Veba AG and Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc.
